newsitem.title: USA: Aris Corp plans initial public offering.
newsitem.headline: Aris Corp plans initial public offering.

text.p: Aris Corp, a Seattle-based computer software services provider, filed documents Thursday indicating it hopes to raise up to $35 million in an initial public offering of its stock.
In the documents filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Aris said it plans to offer up to 2.3 million shares, including overallotments, at $13 to $15 a share.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Montgomery Securities and Piper Jaffray are underwriters.
Aris provides training and consulting, primarily to companies that use Microsoft Corp and Oracle Corp software.
After the offering company founder and Chairman Paul Song and his wife, Tina, will own about 47.4 percent of the company's stock, which will have a total of 9.4 million shares outstanding.
Last year, the six-year-old company had net income of $2 million on revenues of $26.9 million, compared with income of $2 million and revenues of $14.8 million in 1995.
The company has filed to trade on Nasdaq under the symbol ARSC.
